Subject: Request: Full prompt/output + request-log purge for tenant finserve-prod

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for taking the time today. As discussed in the call, FinServe needs a coordinated purge of all customer-provided prompts, model outputs, and request/ingestion logs tied to our production tenant (finserve-prod) for the period Jan 1 2024 — Nov 30 2026. This is a compliance requirement driven by an external audit.

Can you confirm Redwood's steps for:
- scope discovery (where artifacts live: prompt logs, KV caches, derivative embeddings)
- ops execution window and expected downtime (if any)
- certificate/evidence we will receive after deletion
- retention of audit metadata / who will retain the immutable proofchain and where

Attached is our internal scope doc — we've highlighted two urgent buckets. We want a match-to-proof flow so our auditors can sign off.

Appreciate a checklist and an estimated timeline.

Thanks,
Jared
Director, Privacy & Risk
FinServe Inc.

Hi Jared —

Appreciate the clear scope doc. Summary below and an ops checklist attached (redwood-ops-checklist-v2.xlsx). High level: we can execute a scoped purge with no customer-facing downtime; small routing hiccups are possible for active in-flight sessions during the 2-hour execution window.

Planned deliverables (short):
1) Discovery report: list of objects and locations (S3 buckets, KV namespaces, cache shards).
2) Execution plan: step-by-step purge runbook with canary + rollback gates.
3) Evidence package: signed manifest, SHA256 manifest of deleted objects, and a time-stamped stub of the deletion job logs.
4) Audit metadata retention: Redwood will retain immutable job metadata (job id, hashes, operator id) for 2 years per our standard audit retention; no customer prompt outputs or embeddings will be retained after purge unless explicitly excluded.

Questions for you:
- Is there any subset that must be preserved (e.g., redacted copies for regulatory investigations)?
- Preferred blackout window (we've penciled Tue 2026-12-28 03:00–05:00 UTC for low traffic)

Next steps: I'll loop in Ops (marissa) and Compliance (laura) to finalize timing and sign-off template.

Regards,

Hi all —

Ops view and proposed execution plan below. I'll keep this concise; full runbook attached.

Execution summary (proposed):
- Pre-checks (T-72h): asset discovery job runs; operator & job ID issued; change control ticket created (JIRA FIN-PURGE-452).
- Scoped freeze (T-2h): block write access to targeted namespaces, open read-only for verification hooks.
- Canary pass (T+0): run a single-namespace canary purge; validate manifest and hashes; run end-to-end retrievability tests to ensure nothing outside scope is affected.
- Bulk purge (T+30m): parallel deletion workers sweep S3 prefixes, kv-namespace expunger, and request-log index pruner.
- Evidence emission (T+90m): job emits manifest.json with SHA256 per-deleted-object, signed by operator (PGP sig) and job-id; attachment: deletion-evidence-stub.txt (for initial review).
- Post-validation (T+2h): cross-check manifest to discovery report; produce final signed certificate and upload to customer Drive link.

Risk notes:
- Embedding derivatives stored in multi-tenant vector stores will be treated per-tenant: we will remove index entries and recompact shards; this can be slower depending on shard size.
- KV cache TTL vs permanent storage: we will sweep persistent backing stores (not just in-memory caches).

Deliverables & acceptance items for FinServe to confirm:
- Confirm the two highlighted buckets in your scope doc are fully in-scope.
- Confirm blackout window Tue 2026-12-28 03:00–05:00 UTC or propose an alternative.
- Provide the auditor contact for direct evidence handoff (optional).

Attachments: runbook excerpt in redwood-ops-checklist-v2.xlsx; deletion-evidence-stub.txt (text stub of manifest)

Marissa Cole
Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
